result.title: The geometry of neural network decision boundaries
result.summary: Artificial neural networks (ANNs) are built using well-understood mathematical operations, yet their complex nature poses significant challenges to intuitively understanding their decision-making processes. This work introduces a method for visualizing and measuring ANN decision boundary geometry directly in the high-dimensional input space, avoiding distortions found with traditional projection-based techniques. We analyze boundary curvatures and distances in diverse inputs, architectures, and training methods. Boundary distances grow smoothly and slowly with consistent curvature as the size of the subspace increases, suggesting that decision boundaries are close to input samples within large, continuous subspaces. We also quantify how much boundary distances and curvatures reduce near dataset samples after adversarial training. Training methodology has a significantly stronger impact on boundary distance and curvature than architecture or test-set accuracy. These findings are contextualized within prior work, supporting or refuting several previously proposed theories of boundary behavior. Our analytically and empirically supported methodology lays the foundation for future studies to improve network interpretability and understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种在高维输入空间中直接可视化与度量神经网络决策边界几何（边界距离与曲率）的方法，避免投影失真，并在多种输入、架构与训练方式下比较，发现训练方法比架构或测试精度影响更大，对抗训练会显著缩小样本附近的边界距离与曲率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其边界距离与曲率度量或可作为核查 LVR 中 latent 状态几何（如推理状态是否贴近决策边界、表示是否坍缩）的工具线索，但论文限于通用分类网络与输入空间，与 VLM 推理无直接联系，可供核查其度量能否迁移到 latent 轨迹。
